transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alves (Redwood SE), Karen Li (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Halcyon CTO), Liam O'Neill (Halcyon SRE), Sofia Martins (Halcyon ML Eng), Ethan Park (Halcyon Security)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Halcyon is evaluating an exit from mixed OpenAI/Anthropic + in-house vLLM/TGI stack towards either Redwood Hosted to start, then Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
- Primary concerns: eval parity (responses + hallucination), latency budget, cost tradeoffs, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2/ISO compliance, network egress / data residency.
- Agreed next steps: security docs, hosted eval provisioning, parity benchmark plan, SE deep-dive for networking.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're recording this, notes will be sent. quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Rao: yeah hi I'm Priya, CTO at Halcyon. we run a hybrid stack today — we do chat through OpenAI and Anthropic, but for some batch embedding and internal serving we run vLLM + a small TGI-based cluster.
[00:19] Liam O'Neill: Liam, SRE. we maintain the on-prem infra and manage the model ops pipeline.
[00:22] Sofia Martins: Sofia, ML eng. I'm primarily focused on prompt engineering and model comparisons.
[00:25] Maya Chen: great. diego, quick intro?
[00:27] Diego Alves: Diego, SE at Redwood. I focus on latency, batching, and private deploys.
[00:30] Ethan Park: Ethan, security. I'll ask the hard questions about keys and audit logs.
[00:33] Maya Chen: cool, the agenda — hear about your current stack, constraints, what success looks like, and map options: Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private. also parity and benchmarks. sound good?
[00:41] Priya Rao: yep, that covers it.
[00:43] Maya Chen: ok Priya, can you walk us through the current flow and pain points?
[00:47] Priya Rao: sure. so user-facing chat uses OpenAI for low latency, Anthropic for safety checks on certain classes of queries. embeddings for search are done on a vLLM cluster because it's cheaper and we can batch. we've been hitting costs on peak, and the operational overhead of keeping TGI and vLLM updated is increasing. also latency sometimes spikes during autoscaling, so SLA is a concern.
[01:12] Sofia Martins: and parity — we sometimes see behavior drift between OpenAI and our vLLM fine-tuned slices. hallucinations are also a pain, especially for docs-synthesis.
[01:21] Maya Chen: ok makes sense. what are your SLOs?
[01:24] Liam O'Neill: 95th percentile under 120ms for simple chat increments, throughput target 50 rps for our busiest service, embedding batch windows ~1000 docs per job.
[01:36] Diego Alves: 120ms 95th is pretty tight if you're doing heavy context or long sequences. in Redwood we can route low-latency traffic to optimized Hosted instances, we also have Dedicated pools that are tuned for throughput. what models are you running?
[01:48] Sofia Martins: mainly 13B and 7B variants, some experiments with 1B for cheap inference. the vLLM setup uses 4-bit quantization. TGI used for some open-source models.
[01:59] Diego Alves: ok that's helpful. quantization and kernel choices matter a lot for parity and latency. we do an initial perf sweep that chooses kernels and quant paths. sometimes model artifacts from TGI/vllm conversions — excuse me — vLLM conversions require tokenizer alignment.
[02:16] Priya Rao: tokenizer alignment has bitten us. sometimes metrics look fine but outputs differ subtly. we want to make sure we can run parity tests.
[02:22] Maya Chen: absolutely. our SEs can run an apples-to-apples parity benchmark: same prompts, same temperature/top-p, capture ngram overlap, hallucination counts, latency percentiles. diego will own the perf plan.
[02:33] Diego Alves: yes I'll draft a benchmark plan. quick question — are you leaning towards Hosted first or go straight to Private?
[02:39] Priya Rao: preference is Hosted for quick time-to-value, but private for regulatory customers. long term we expect Dedicated or Private. the path matters: we don't want to do double work migrating twice.
[02:50] Maya Chen: totally fair. our typical approach is Hosted eval, then Dedicated sizing and finally Private VPC or on-prem packaging once the PoC stabilizes. we provide config continuity so canary policies and rollouts map across.
[03:03] Ethan Park: security — we need SOC2 type II, SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration with our HSM provider. can you support customer-managed KMS?
[03:14] Diego Alves: yes, Private deployments support KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted supports envelope encryption and integrates with common KMS providers; for full customer-managed HSM we'd usually recommend Private.
[03:25] Ethan Park: and key rotation / separation of duties?
[03:27] Diego Alves: yes, we can integrate with KMS rotation policies and RBAC. logs are exportable to your SIEM.
[03:32] Priya Rao: any gotchas on data residency and egress charges?
[03:35] Maya Chen: Hosted is region-aware; we can provision in EU/US regions. Dedicated offers more control over network egress and peering. Private gives you full control. we can produce an egress estimate once we see traffic profiles.
[03:46] Sofia Martins: about eval parity — can Redwood run a blind test vs OpenAI/Anthropic to see if the outputs match quality levels? we want to show product stakeholders.
[03:55] Diego Alves: yes. we run side-by-side comparisons. caveat: some provider-specific safety layers or prompting wrappers can cause differences. we can replicate temperature/top-p and prompt engineering exactly, but upstream proprietary model behaviors differ.
[04:09] Priya Rao: understood. for hallucination detection we use a set of gold prompts and human labeling on a sample of 500 prompts. will that be enough?
[04:17] Diego Alves: 500 is a solid start; we recommend stratifying by prompt length and intent type. we'll instrument automated heuristics too.
[04:23] Maya Chen: let's talk cost. you mentioned spikes — what's your current spend pattern?
[04:27] Priya Rao: monthly across providers ~ $120k on API ops plus infra for vLLM at about $30k for maintenance and GPUs.
[04:35] Maya Chen: ok. Dedicated can lower unit cost but has commit/size tradeoffs. Redwood Optimize provides batching and cache configs that can reduce per-token costs substantially.
[04:45] Sofia Martins: will caching affect freshness? we often need latest docs synthesis so prefix caching needs careful TTLs.
[04:51] Diego Alves: yep, prefix/KV caching can be tuned by route. we support eviction and TTLs per-route.
[04:56] Liam O'Neill: what about model variants and automatic fallback? if a big model is down we can't have user-facing outages.
[05:02] Diego Alves: we have smart routing policies: fallback to cheaper model variants or region fallback. canary deploys and automatic rollback on error rates.
[05:10] Maya Chen: also feature flags so you can route a percent of traffic to Redwood while keeping a portion on your current provider during ramp.
[05:16] Priya Rao: nice. network setup for Private — do you support direct connect/peering?
[05:20] Diego Alves: yes, for Dedicated we support private peering and VPC setups; for Private we package an on-prem agent and can set up direct connect tunnels.
[05:28] Ethan Park: we need end-to-end encryption in transit + at rest. any plaintext logging?
[05:32] Diego Alves: no plaintext. logs can be redacted, and access to logs is RBAC controlled. we can provide an audit log export for compliance.
[05:40] Priya Rao: great, let's talk timeline. we have a Q1 2027 push to reduce vendor cost and have one control plane. ideal runbook?
[05:48] Maya Chen: typical is Week 0: PoC scoping, Week 1-2: Hosted eval with sample prompts, Week 3: benchmark analysis and Dedicated sizing, Week 4-6: Dedicated pilot or Private prep.
[05:59] Sofia Martins: how long to get a Hosted eval project?
[06:01] Maya Chen: we can spin a trial project in 48 hours once we have sample prompts and API keys. Diego will need sample payloads for benchmarking.
[06:09] Diego Alves: yup I'll send an example harness. also need seq length distribution and typical batch sizes.
[06:13] Priya Rao: about tuning — do you handle quantization profiles or do we need to re-quantize?
[06:18] Diego Alves: we support a set of quant profiles and can accept your 4-bit artifacts; sometimes a repack/convert step is needed. we'll document any differences.
[06:26] Maya Chen: ok let's surface risks: Priya, what keeps you up at night?
[06:29] Priya Rao: main risk is parity and user regressions. execs want a clear measurement that product quality won't degrade. second is data residency and keys. third is the migration effort.
[06:38] Maya Chen: fair. for parity we propose a blind A/B with human raters and automated diff metrics, plus rolling canary. for migration effort, we offer migration guides and SE support; many customers do Hosted eval first to prove parity.
[06:50] Ethan Park: any SOC2/ISO certs we can review?
[06:53] Maya Chen: yes, I'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO docs, and the security whitepaper.
[06:57] Liam O'Neill: what about telemetry and costs breakdown? we need token-level cost and route breakdowns to show the finance team.
[07:04] Maya Chen: Redwood Console gives per-route token costs, latency heatmaps, and model breakdowns. we'll include screenshots in the follow-up.
[07:11] Sofia Martins: one more technical — how do you manage KV cache for multi-turn sessions? we rely heavily on KV caching to avoid recompute.
[07:18] Diego Alves: we manage KV/Caching per-session with TTLs and can pin KV to shards for locality. for Dedicated we expose cache controls you can tune.
[07:27] Priya Rao: great. any constraints on model licensing for open-source models?
[07:31] Maya Chen: we respect upstream licenses and can advise on which models are redistribution-friendly. for private deployments we provide the tooling to host models you are licensed to run.
[07:40] Ethan Park: final question — will Redwood run a benchmark against OpenAI's Chat for us, or do we need to provide an account?
[07:45] Diego Alves: we can run black-box parity using public endpoints, but for apples-to-apples we'll need any proprietary prompt wrappers you use or telemetries; ideally we get an OpenAI/Anthropic account you can provide for the test window.
[07:57] Priya Rao: we'll see what security allows but ok.
[08:00] Maya Chen: wrap up — recap of next steps: Maya to send security docs and pricing; Diego to send benchmark plan and harness; Priya to share prompt set and SLOs; Ethan to confirm KMS provider. schedule SE deep dive for 2027-01-06.
[08:14] Priya Rao: sounds good, thanks all.
[08:16] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links. bye.

End of transcript.
